characterized_levers.name: Participant Recruitment Channels
characterized_levers.consequences: Expanding recruitment channels increases participant flow, potentially accelerating enrollment and event capture. However, broader recruitment may introduce heterogeneity in the participant pool, requiring more stringent screening and potentially affecting the generalizability of findings. Overly broad recruitment can also strain resources allocated for screening and onboarding.
options: Actively recruit through national patient advocacy groups and online forums dedicated to sleep disorders, emphasizing the potential for personalized feedback and contributing to scientific advancement.

Establish a collaborative referral network with general practitioners and community health centers in the Bonn metropolitan area, offering educational seminars on parasomnia recognition and referral pathways.

Partner with local media outlets to run public service announcements and feature stories about the research unit, raising awareness and encouraging self-referral from individuals experiencing parasomnia symptoms.
characterized_levers.review: Expanding recruitment boosts enrollment speed, but introduces selection biases; the options neglect proactive engagement with underserved populations who may lack access to traditional channels.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: Participant recruitment is important for enrollment targets, but the specific channels are secondary to the overall recruitment strategy and inclusion/exclusion criteria.
characterized_levers.description: Participant Recruitment Channels define the pathways through which eligible participants are identified and enrolled. Options include the University Hospital Bonn sleep clinic (internal referrals), regional neurologists (external clinical networks), and the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Schlafforschung und Schlafmedizin (national sleep society network). Each channel has different reach, screening quality, referrer familiarity with inclusion/exclusion criteria, and logistical friction. Success metrics are meeting enrollment targets (50–70 by month 36), maintaining at least 70–80% event-capture rate, minimizing protocol violations, and achieving demographic diversity. Diversified channels reduce dependence on single bottleneck.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Multi-channel recruitment synergizes powerfully with Suite Ambient Design and Pharmaceutical Partnership outcomes. Diverse referral sources (clinical networks, sleep society) increase brand visibility and recruitment momentum, particularly if publications and institutional prestige accelerate. Domestic suite aesthetics appeal to broader participant profiles (anxious, claustrophobic candidates excluded from clinical labs), expanding the recruitment pool. Partnership announcements via pharma connections can amplify awareness within clinical networks without compromising academic independence.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Recruitment channels conflict with rigorous pre-admission screening. Open DGzSS network channels may refer participants with inadequate pre-screening, increasing protocol violations (unconfirmed parasomnias, cryptic epilepsy) and reducing usable cohort fraction. External neurologist referrals lack direct access to detailed history-taking, raising exclusion errors (e.g., undetected sleep apnea). High recruitment pressure to meet 50–70 targets creates incentive to relax entry criteria, conflicting with Participant Recruitment accuracy and the need for a truly confirmed NREM parasomnia cohort for valid Aim 2 phenotyping.

characterized_levers.name: Overnight Staffing Model
characterized_levers.consequences: The overnight staffing model directly impacts participant safety, event capture rates, and technician workload. Increasing staff improves response time to events and annotation throughput, but raises personnel costs. Reducing staff may compromise safety and data quality, particularly if multiple events occur simultaneously.
options: Implement a hybrid staffing model where a single technician remotely monitors multiple suites via video and sensor data, with a second technician on-call for immediate in-person response to flagged events.
Cross-train research staff from the Department of Epileptology to provide supplemental overnight coverage during peak periods, leveraging existing expertise and reducing the need for dedicated hires.
Introduce a tiered response protocol where automated alerts trigger graduated levels of intervention, from remote observation to in-person assessment, optimizing technician time allocation.
characterized_levers.review: Adjusting staffing balances cost and responsiveness, but the options overlook the potential for burnout and attrition associated with demanding overnight shifts.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: The overnight staffing model directly impacts participant safety, data quality, and the ability to respond to events, making it a core strategic decision.
characterized_levers.description: Overnight Staffing Model determines the composition, scheduling, training, and roles of night-shift personnel. It controls the ratio of technicians to active suites (plan mandates 3 technicians covering 8 suites safely), whether technicians are multi-skilled (EEG, safety response, video monitoring) or specialized, scheduling patterns (fixed vs. rotating), cross-training depth, and shift handover protocols. Success metrics are safe event response, minimal false alarms, technician retention and morale, real-time data quality assurance, and Annotation Review Depth support. Adequate staffing is essential for participant safety and event capture; understaffing compromises both.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: The 3-technician model for 8 suites synergizes with Nocturnal Safety Protocol and Data Acquisition Triggering. Adequate coverage enables real-time video and audio monitoring for technician-observation-based escalation, reducing response latency for safety concerns and maximizing behavioral event capture before suppression. Rotating shifts with cross-training allow experienced staff to mentor newer team members, improving Technician Training Focus and building institutional knowledge. This staffing cushion also enables one technician to respond to an acute event while others maintain monitoring continuity.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: The 3:8 ratio is tight and conflicts with projected growth or unplanned absences. If a technician is ill or departs unexpectedly, effective coverage drops to 2:8, violating safety margins and forcing reduced occupancy. This creates tension with enrollment targets: to hit 50–70 participants by month 36, occupancy must average 4–5 concurrent participants per week; understaffing forces slower enrollment. Intensive technician duties (real-time monitoring, event flagging, initial annotation, safety response) conflict with focused Annotation Review Depth—technicians fatigued from night shifts may produce lower-quality preliminary flags, overburdening daytime dual-review scorers and slowing event adjudication cycles.

characterized_levers.name: Data Acquisition Pipeline
characterized_levers.consequences: The data acquisition pipeline determines the richness and fidelity of captured data, influencing the accuracy of event characterization and the performance of event-triage tools. Increasing sensor density and sampling rates improves data resolution, but also increases storage requirements, annotation burden, and computational complexity. Reducing data volume eases processing demands but may sacrifice critical information.
options: Implement adaptive sampling rates that dynamically adjust data acquisition based on real-time event detection, increasing resolution during suspected parasomnia episodes and reducing it during periods of quiescence.
Prioritize specific sensor modalities based on their predictive power for parasomnia events, reducing the reliance on less informative channels and streamlining the data stream.
Integrate automated artifact detection and removal algorithms into the data pipeline, minimizing the need for manual cleaning and improving the efficiency of subsequent analysis.
characterized_levers.review: Modifying the data pipeline trades off data richness against processing efficiency, but the options do not address the potential for introducing systematic biases through automated pre-processing steps.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: The data acquisition pipeline determines the quality and type of data collected, which is fundamental to achieving the research aims.
characterized_levers.description: This lever governs the sensor and data-stream strategy: full continuous recording at fixed resolution, adaptive sampling adjusting rates based on detected events, sensor prioritization downweighting uninformative channels, or automated artifact cleaning. It directly controls data quality, storage/compute burden, annotation efficiency, and feasibility of subsequent analysis. Success metrics include inter-rater reliability on scored segments, reconstruction fidelity of detected events, and tractability of downstream computational phenotyping without excessive missing data or artifacts.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Tight synergy with Event Detection Automation and Data Acquisition Triggering. Adaptive sampling triggered by real-time event detection (low resolution during quiescence, high resolution post-flag) directly feeds semi-automated triage tools, reducing annotation burden while preserving clinical-grade signal during likely parasomnia events. Automated artifact removal similarly amplifies the signal-to-noise ratio available for machine-learning event detection, improving algorithm sensitivity and specificity, which in turn benchmarks stronger against the dual human-rater gold standard.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Trade-off between data completeness and operational efficiency. Adaptive sampling and sensor prioritization risk missing infrequent parasomnia precursors or atypical morphologies that fall outside the learned detection thresholds, biasing Aim 2 longitudinal characterization toward 'typical' events. Aggressive artifact removal may discard genuine physiological signal misclassified as noise. Conversely, continuous full-resolution recording on all sensors ensures no loss but inflates storage (terabytes/month), compute, and annotation overhead, constraining the number of participants and research depth within fixed budget.

characterized_levers.name: Event Adjudication Protocol
characterized_levers.consequences: The event adjudication protocol directly affects the reliability and validity of the identified parasomnia events. More rigorous adjudication, such as requiring consensus from multiple expert raters, improves accuracy but increases scoring costs and turnaround time. Less stringent adjudication reduces costs but may compromise data quality.
options: Employ a machine-learning model pre-trained on a large dataset of polysomnography recordings to pre-screen potential events, reducing the number of segments requiring manual review by expert raters.
Implement a 'disagreement resolution' pathway where a third, senior expert adjudicates only those events on which the initial two raters disagree, focusing resources on the most ambiguous cases.
Establish a standardized training program for raters, incorporating regular calibration exercises and feedback sessions to minimize inter-rater variability and improve overall agreement.
characterized_levers.review: Adjusting adjudication stringency balances accuracy and cost, but the options fail to consider the potential for rater fatigue and the impact of subjective biases on event classification.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: The event adjudication protocol directly impacts the reliability and validity of the identified parasomnia events, a core element of the research.
characterized_levers.description: Event Adjudication Protocol defines the formal process for confirming whether a flagged sensor event or technician observation meets criteria for a true parasomnia episode versus a confound, normal arousal, or epileptic mimic. It controls the decision framework (AASM criteria strictness, clinical judgment input, specialist review escalation), the adjudicators' qualifications (sleep medicine physician PI vs. trained technician consensus), and the documentation standard. Success metrics include reproducibility across raters, defense against ethics board scrutiny, scientific publication credibility, and participant safety (excluding true epilepsy mimics). Rigorous adjudication is essential for Aim 2 characterization and Aim 3 automation benchmarking.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Rigorous adjudication synergizes strongly with Annotation Review Depth and Event Detection Automation benchmarking. A structured protocol with physician PI review (adjudicating borderline or high-risk events) combined with dual-technician scoring ensures high-quality ground truth. This dual-level review cascade—technician flags, dual annotation, PI adjudication for disputes—maximizes sensitivity while preserving specificity. Clean adjudicated events become the gold standard for training and evaluating automated detection, directly enabling Aim 3 success.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Strict physician-led adjudication creates bottleneck and cost burden. The PI reviewing every flagged event as arbiter slows turnaround, delays publications, and increases labor cost (PI time is expensive). Overly stringent AASM criterion adherence may exclude clinically relevant but borderline episodes, reducing event yield and Aim 2 phenotypic diversity. Conversely, loose adjudication (technician consensus without physician oversight) risks including epileptic seizures or other mimics, creating ethics and safety liability. Escalation to external sleep medicine experts for dispute resolution adds cost and delays; avoiding escalation risks false positives contaminating the Event Detection Automation training dataset.

characterized_levers.name: Pharmaceutical Partnership Terms
characterized_levers.consequences: Securing a pharmaceutical industry partnership provides additional funding and potential access to proprietary compounds or technologies. However, it may also introduce conflicts of interest, restrict publication timelines, or influence the research agenda. Maintaining academic independence is crucial for preserving scientific integrity.
options: Negotiate a 'blinded' collaboration where the pharmaceutical partner provides funding and access to compounds, but remains unaware of participant-level data or specific research hypotheses until after publication.

Establish a clear 'firewall' between the academic research team and the pharmaceutical partner's marketing or product development divisions, ensuring that research findings are not used for promotional purposes.
Structure the partnership as a 'research consortium' involving multiple pharmaceutical companies, diversifying funding sources and reducing the influence of any single partner on the research agenda.
characterized_levers.review: Pharma partnerships offer funding but risk compromising research independence; the options neglect the potential for intellectual property disputes or restrictions on data sharing.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: Pharmaceutical partnership terms are important for funding and collaboration, but the project's feasibility doesn't hinge on it, making it secondary.
characterized_levers.description: Pharmaceutical Partnership Terms defines the scope, governance, and incentive structure for industry collaboration. Key dimensions include publication rights (full academic independence vs. company veto), data access (academic-only vs. shared), financial dependency (optional bonus vs. critical funding pillar), timeline alignment (academic-paced vs. commercial milestones), and IP ownership. The plan mandates that pharma remain optional upside—not a feasibility requirement—and that academics retain full publication authority with pharma receiving only a 30-day pre-publication comment window. Success metrics are securing funding without compromising scientific independence, avoiding publication delays, maintaining ethics board approval, and preserving team morale.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Partnership terms synergize with Publication Target Breadth and Data Sharing Scope. A structured 30-day comment window preserves timely publication in peer-reviewed sleep medicine journals while acknowledging pharma interests. Open data sharing under DUAs (excluding video) aligns with transparent science and academic credibility. If industry funding is secured, restricted publication rights are avoided, enabling the 2–3 papers required by success criteria and boosting recruitment through institutional prestige without perception of commercial capture.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Deep industry partnership conflicts with research independence and timeline autonomy. If pharma becomes a primary funding pillar (counter to plan), company milestones (e.g., compound development phases) may pressure publication delays or demand data exclusivity, violating success criteria (peer-reviewed publications by month 36). Patent or IP claims on event-triage algorithms would conflict with open-science principles and Data Sharing Scope. Mandatory commercial secrecy also conflicts with Technician Training Focus: external collaborators and trainees cannot engage if data is proprietary, limiting workforce development and reproducibility.

characterized_levers.name: Residential Suite Configuration
characterized_levers.consequences: The configuration of the residential suites impacts participant comfort, safety, and data quality. More elaborate suites with advanced monitoring capabilities increase costs and complexity. Simpler suites reduce costs but may limit the range of observable behaviors and compromise participant comfort.
options: Designate a subset of suites as 'high-fidelity' rooms equipped with advanced sensor arrays and environmental controls, reserving them for participants with complex or high-risk parasomnia profiles.
Incorporate modular design elements into the suites, allowing for flexible reconfiguration based on individual participant needs and research protocols.
Prioritize participant comfort and domesticity by incorporating personalized lighting, soundscapes, and bedding options into each suite, fostering a more relaxed and naturalistic sleep environment.
characterized_levers.review: Suite configuration balances data capture and participant comfort, but the options overlook the potential for the suites themselves to influence sleep patterns and introduce artificiality.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: Residential suite configuration impacts participant comfort and data quality, but is secondary to the overall safety and data acquisition strategies.
characterized_levers.description: Residential Suite Configuration determines the physical and technological differentiation of sleep monitoring spaces. This lever controls whether suites are uniform or stratified by participant complexity, whether modular reconfiguration is available, and how personalization balances domesticity against standardization. Success metrics include participant comfort retention (reducing suppression of naturalistic behavior), equipment utilization efficiency, and safety margins for high-risk profiles. The choice directly impacts recruitment viability, technician workload, and data quality consistency across the cohort.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This lever strongly synergizes with Suite Ambient Design and Nocturnal Safety Protocol. Modular, comfort-prioritized suite configuration enables the domestic aesthetic of Suite Ambient Design to flourish, reducing clinical atmosphere that suppresses parasomnias. It also supports tiered Safety Protocol by allowing high-fidelity rooms designated for complex cases, where enhanced sensor arrays and environmental controls enable safer, more precise intervention matching.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: High-fidelity suite stratification conflicts with equitable recruitment and operational simplicity. Designating premium suites for complex profiles may stigmatize or deter participants, while modular flexibility increases technician training demands and introduces configuration variance that challenges Event Detection Automation and annotation consistency. Personalization options can compromise the standardized reference baseline needed for control group comparison.

characterized_levers.name: Suite Ambient Design
characterized_levers.consequences: The aesthetic and functional design of the residential suites directly impacts participant comfort and naturalistic behavior. A more clinical environment may increase participant anxiety and suppress parasomnia events, while an overly permissive environment could compromise safety. Balancing these factors is crucial for data quality and participant retention.
options: Prioritize a highly domestic aesthetic with soft lighting, familiar furniture, and personalized decor to encourage relaxation and natural sleep patterns
Implement a minimalist design with standardized layouts, neutral colors, and easily cleanable surfaces to facilitate efficient monitoring and minimize potential hazards
Offer participants a choice between several pre-designed suite themes, balancing domestic comfort with research requirements and allowing for some personalization
characterized_levers.review: A homelike suite design risks compromising data quality and safety, while a clinical design may inhibit natural behavior; the gap is a design that adapts to individual participant needs.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: Suite ambient design is important for participant comfort and naturalistic behavior, but is secondary to the core safety and data acquisition strategies.
characterized_levers.description: Suite Ambient Design governs the aesthetic, sensory, and psychosocial environment of residential monitoring spaces. It controls lighting warmth, furniture familiarity, decor personalization, color schemes, and cleanability—directly influencing whether participants relax into naturalistic nocturnal behavior or remain hyper-aware of the research setting. Success metrics are reduced sleep latency, lower arousals during adaptation nights, qualitative comfort ratings, and whether captured parasomnia morphology matches clinical presentation outside the facility. A domestic feel is scientifically essential; overly clinical environments suppress infrequent events.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Domestic ambient design synergizes powerfully with Participant Recruitment Channels and Nocturnal Safety Protocol. Warm, personalized aesthetics increase recruitment appeal and retention, particularly for anxious or claustrophobic candidates screening out of clinical labs. It also enables the 'hands-off' or verbal-redirection safety model: a home-like setting with lower alertness cues allows technicians to monitor unobtrusively without triggering environmental awareness that suppresses parasomnia expression.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Domestic design directly conflicts with standardization and infection control priorities embedded in minimalist approaches. Personalized decor increases cleaning burden, storage complexity, and potential biohazard vectors; familiar furniture compromises the hygienic baseline required for participant safety and data comparability. Customization also conflicts with efficient Data Acquisition Triggering—heterogeneous room layouts and furniture placement complicate consistent video-based behavior recognition and event flagging.

characterized_levers.name: Nocturnal Safety Protocol
characterized_levers.consequences: Safety protocols dictate the level of intervention during parasomnia events. Overly restrictive protocols may prevent the capture of complete events or introduce artificial awakenings, while insufficient protocols could expose participants to injury. The balance between safety and data integrity is paramount.
options: Implement a 'hands-off' approach, intervening only in cases of imminent danger as determined by pre-defined escalation criteria and real-time video monitoring
Establish a tiered intervention system, starting with verbal redirection and escalating to physical intervention only if necessary to prevent injury
Employ a proactive safety model with frequent room checks and sensor-triggered alerts to preemptively address potential hazards before escalation
characterized_levers.review: Strict safety protocols can disrupt natural sleep and parasomnia events, while lax protocols increase injury risk; the gap is a protocol that dynamically adjusts to individual risk profiles.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: Nocturnal safety protocol is a primary concern, as it directly impacts participant well-being and the ethical conduct of the research.
characterized_levers.description: Nocturnal Safety Protocol defines the intervention philosophy and trigger thresholds for technician response to parasomnia episodes. It controls whether staff intervene minimally (only imminent danger), tiered (verbal first, physical if needed), or proactively (frequent checks, sensor alerts). Success metrics include zero serious injuries, maintained participant dignity and autonomy, event capture without suppression, technician stress and false-alarm burden, and ethical defensibility to ethics boards and families. The protocol must balance participant safety against the risk that overt monitoring suppresses the very events being studied.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Tiered or hands-off safety protocols synergize with domestic ambient design and realistic Suite Configuration. A relaxed, home-like setting with minimal visible intervention enables naturalistic behavior and parasomnia expression, while tiered escalation ensures dignified, proportional response. Combined with selective high-fidelity suites for complex profiles, safety is preserved without constant intrusion that would suppress events or violate autonomy.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Proactive safety (frequent checks, sensor alerts) conflicts sharply with Event Detection Automation and naturalistic behavior capture. Continuous room checks and alert-triggered presence suppress the unremarkable sleep environment necessary for parasomnias to occur; excessive intervention also generates noise and light disturbance flagged as confounds. Tension also exists with Technician Training Focus: hands-off models require expert real-time judgment, whereas proactive systems demand consistent procedural adherence across all staff regardless of experience.

characterized_levers.name: Data Acquisition Triggering
characterized_levers.consequences: The method for triggering enhanced data acquisition (full PSG) influences the richness and relevance of the captured data. Relying solely on scheduled nights may miss critical events, while continuous full PSG is resource-intensive and uncomfortable for participants. A hybrid approach is needed to optimize data yield.
options: Trigger enhanced PSG based on real-time technician observation of unusual behavior via video and audio monitoring, capturing events as they unfold
Schedule enhanced PSG nights based on participant-reported event frequency and timing, maximizing the likelihood of capturing typical episodes
Utilize machine-learning algorithms to detect potential parasomnia events from low-burden sensor data, triggering enhanced PSG automatically based on probability scores
characterized_levers.review: Technician-triggered PSG is subjective, participant-scheduled PSG relies on recall, and algorithm-triggered PSG depends on model accuracy; the gap is a multi-modal triggering system.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: Data acquisition triggering determines when enhanced data is collected, directly impacting the ability to capture and characterize parasomnia events.
characterized_levers.description: Data Acquisition Triggering controls when enhanced polysomnography (full scalp EEG, EOG, chin/leg EMG) is deployed beyond the three scheduled nights. Options include real-time technician observation of unusual behavior, pre-scheduled nights based on reported history, or automated machine-learning detection from low-burden sensors. Success metrics are capture rate of adjudicated events, false-positive escalation burden, technician cognitive load, and sensitivity relative to ground-truth parasomnia occurrence. Optimal triggering maximizes event yield while minimizing wasted enhanced recordings and technician fatigue.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Real-time technician observation triggering synergizes strongly with Event Detection Automation and Annotation Review Depth. A trained technician flagging behavior in the moment provides ground-truth labels for training and validating automated detection systems, accelerating algorithm development. Combined with thorough annotation review, these create a virtuous cycle: technician judgment informs automation, which refines technician focus, improving dual-scorer adjudication quality and event-triage model benchmarking.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Automated machine-learning triggering conflicts with the methodological principle that autonomous diagnosis is banned and dual human adjudication is mandatory. Over-reliance on algorithms to decide enhanced PSG deployment risks circularity: the model selects events it is trained to recognize, potentially missing novel morphologies and biasing the dataset. Additionally, frequent automated escalations conflict with naturalistic monitoring—alert overhead and technician response disrupt sleep and suppress event expression. Participant-reported history triggering conflicts with Event Detection Automation by avoiding the sensor-data ground truth needed to train detection models.

characterized_levers.name: Event Detection Automation
characterized_levers.consequences: The level of automation in event detection impacts the efficiency of data processing and the accuracy of event identification. Fully automated systems may generate false positives or miss subtle events, while manual review is time-consuming and prone to human error. A balanced approach is essential.
options: Develop a rule-based system using pre-defined physiological and behavioral criteria to automatically flag potential parasomnia events for further review
Train a deep-learning model on a large dataset of annotated parasomnia events to automatically detect and classify episodes with high accuracy
Employ a hybrid approach combining rule-based flagging with machine-learning classification to leverage the strengths of both methods
characterized_levers.review: Rule-based systems lack nuance, deep-learning models require extensive training data, and hybrid approaches inherit the limitations of both; the gap is a system that adapts to data heterogeneity.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: Event detection automation is important for data processing efficiency, but is secondary to the core data acquisition and adjudication strategies.
characterized_levers.description: Event Detection Automation governs the strategy for identifying probable parasomnia episodes in multi-modal sensor streams, reducing manual review burden. Options span rule-based criteria, deep-learning classification, or hybrid approaches. Success metrics include sensitivity and specificity relative to dual human scorer agreement (not autonomous diagnosis), inter-rater reliability improvement, technician time savings, and generalizability across participant heterogeneity. The tool must be benchmarked transparently; overfitting to the development cohort is a critical failure mode. Automation serves triage, not replacement, of human judgment.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Hybrid rule-based plus machine-learning automation synergizes powerfully with Annotation Review Depth and Data Acquisition Triggering. Rule-based systems capture clear physiological markers (e.g., EMG bursts, arousal clusters), while ML refines edge cases and morphological variants. Coupled with rigorous dual-reviewer annotation and real-time technician flagging, this dual-path approach accelerates learning: clear cases inform rule refinement, ambiguous cases improve ML generalization, and all decisions remain grounded in human adjudication consensus.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Deep-learning models conflict with the prohibition on autonomous diagnosis and the small-cohort reality (50–70 participants yields ~40–60 events—insufficient for robust CNN training without severe overfitting). Over-ambitious automation also conflicts with Annotation Review Depth: if technicians trust an automated classifier, they may lower scrutiny, reducing the high-quality dual-scored ground truth the model requires. Rule-based systems conflict with capturing novel or rare parasomnia morphologies outside pre-defined criteria, potentially biasing event characterization toward frequent phenotypes.

characterized_levers.name: Annotation Review Depth
characterized_levers.consequences: The intensity of manual review affects the reliability and validity of event scoring. Single-rater scoring is efficient but susceptible to bias, while multi-rater scoring is more robust but resource-intensive. The optimal balance depends on the study's specific aims and resources.
options: Implement a single-rater scoring system with periodic inter-rater reliability checks to ensure consistency and minimize bias
Employ a dual-rater scoring system with adjudication of disagreements by a senior sleep medicine physician to maximize accuracy
Utilize a tiered review process, with automated pre-screening followed by targeted manual review of ambiguous or high-priority events
characterized_levers.review: Single-rater scoring risks bias, dual-rater scoring is costly, and tiered review depends on pre-screening accuracy; the gap is a review process that adapts to event complexity.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: Annotation review depth directly impacts the reliability and validity of event scoring, a core element of the research.
characterized_levers.description: Annotation Review Depth governs the rigor and personnel required for event scoring against AASM criteria. The dual-rater system with adjudication by a senior sleep medicine physician maximizes diagnostic accuracy and inter-rater reliability reporting, essential for Aim 3's benchmarking of semi-automated tools against human consensus. This approach directly supports publications requiring high methodological credibility. Trade-offs include increased technician labor, longer turnaround for scoring, and higher costs per event, but quality is non-negotiable for clinical validity.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Dual-rater scoring directly strengthens Event Adjudication Protocol by providing robust gold-standard event labels. It also synergizes with Event Detection Automation, as higher-quality human consensus enables better model training and clearer sensitivity/specificity benchmarking. Strong inter-rater reporting also supports Publication Target Breadth by yielding methodologically rigorous manuscripts.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Dual-rater scoring increases personnel costs and manual review time, constraining Overnight Staffing Model flexibility and budget allocation. It also tensions with Event-Triage Confidence Threshold—higher thresholds reduce flagged events for dual review, lowering annotation workload but potentially underutilizing rater capacity and slowing algorithm refinement.

characterized_levers.name: Data Sharing Scope
characterized_levers.consequences: The extent of data sharing influences the impact and reproducibility of the research. Openly sharing all data maximizes transparency but raises privacy concerns, while restricting data sharing limits the potential for collaboration and validation. A carefully considered data-sharing policy is crucial.
options: Share only de-identified physiological data and summary statistics through a secure data repository with restricted access and data use agreements
Establish a collaborative data-sharing platform with select research partners, providing access to more detailed data under strict confidentiality agreements
Publish fully anonymized datasets with synthetic data augmentation to protect participant privacy while maximizing data utility
characterized_levers.review: Restricted data sharing limits collaboration, open sharing risks privacy breaches, and synthetic data may distort findings; the gap is a data-sharing model that balances access and privacy.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: Data sharing scope is important for reproducibility and collaboration, but is secondary to the core research aims and participant privacy.
characterized_levers.description: Data Sharing Scope determines what physiological and sensor data are deposited publicly versus restricted to collaborators, balancing scientific impact and participant privacy. The plan explicitly excludes bedroom video from public repositories due to privacy constraints and prioritizes de-identified physiological data under data use agreements. This lever controls reproducibility, secondary research access, and regulatory compliance. Scope decisions affect publication reach, collaboration network growth, and long-term data utility for future parasomnia research.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Restricted sharing of de-identified physiological data aligns with Pharmaceutical Partnership Terms, enabling secure pharma access for biomarker exploration while protecting participant privacy. It also enhances Publication Target Breadth by allowing methodologically transparent data documentation alongside peer-reviewed outputs, increasing citation and reuse potential without exposing sensitive information.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Restrictive data sharing limits open-science adoption and secondary-use research, constraining Publication Target Breadth and community engagement. Collaborative platform expansion conflicts with tight privacy governance and ethics approval constraints; wider data access increases de-identification liability and administrative overhead, competing for limited study coordinator and legal resources.

characterized_levers.name: Environmental Cue Management
characterized_levers.consequences: Carefully managing environmental cues can either promote or disrupt natural sleep patterns. Introducing specific light or sound stimuli could trigger or suppress parasomnia events, but may also alter sleep architecture and reduce the ecological validity of the data. A balance must be struck to maximize event capture without fundamentally changing the sleep environment.
options: Implement a fixed schedule of light and temperature changes to standardize the sleep environment and minimize external influences on sleep patterns
Introduce personalized pre-sleep routines based on participant habits to promote relaxation and natural sleep onset, while carefully documenting any deviations
Randomize exposure to subtle auditory or olfactory stimuli during sleep to probe for potential triggers of parasomnia events, while monitoring for habituation effects
characterized_levers.review: Standardizing environmental cues may reduce variability but also suppress naturalistic behaviors, and the options neglect the potential for participant-driven environmental adjustments.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: Environmental cue management can influence sleep patterns, but is secondary to the core safety and data acquisition strategies.
characterized_levers.description: Environmental Cue Management controls whether sleep conditions are standardized, personalized, or experimentally probed for parasomnia triggers. Standardized light and temperature optimize cross-participant comparability for Aim 2 phenotyping. Personalized routines maximize naturalistic behavior and participant comfort, preserving the domestic feel critical to avoiding suppression of parasomnia expression. Experimental stimulus probing risks disrupting sleep and triggering events unpredictably, complicating safety and data interpretation but potentially revealing trigger mechanisms.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Personalized pre-sleep routines strongly synergize with Suite Ambient Design by creating a comfortable domestic environment that elicits natural parasomnia expression. This approach also supports Nocturnal Safety Protocol by enabling technicians to anticipate individualized sleep patterns and adjust monitoring sensitivity accordingly, improving event capture and safety margins.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Personalized routines reduce environmental standardization, limiting cross-participant comparability and complicating Aim 2 statistical analysis of within-person versus between-person patterns. Experimental stimulus probing directly conflicts with Nocturnal Safety Protocol by introducing controlled triggers that may precipitate unpredictable or severe parasomnia events, increasing injury risk and technician intervention demands.

characterized_levers.name: Technician Training Focus
characterized_levers.consequences: The training focus for overnight technicians directly impacts both participant safety and data quality. Prioritizing safety protocols minimizes risk but may reduce time spent on detailed annotation. Conversely, emphasizing annotation accuracy could compromise vigilance in responding to participant events.
options: Prioritize comprehensive safety training, including de-escalation techniques and emergency response protocols, to ensure participant well-being above all else
Emphasize real-time annotation skills and AASM scoring criteria to maximize the accuracy and completeness of event logging during overnight shifts
Implement a blended training approach that balances safety protocols with basic annotation skills, supplemented by remote expert support for complex events
characterized_levers.review: Balancing safety and annotation skills requires a trade-off, and the options overlook the potential for specialized roles focusing on either safety or annotation.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: Technician training focus directly impacts both participant safety and data quality, making it a core strategic decision.
characterized_levers.description: Technician Training Focus determines whether night-shift personnel prioritize safety and de-escalation, real-time AASM scoring accuracy, or a balanced hybrid. Safety-first training minimizes participant injury and liability, core to Aim 1 operational validation. Annotation-focused training maximizes in-the-moment event logging quality, reducing downstream dual-rater burden and accelerating algorithm development. A blended approach with remote expert support balances both but requires infrastructure and availability of on-call senior staff during overnight hours.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Safety-first training directly supports Nocturnal Safety Protocol by equipping technicians with de-escalation and emergency skills essential for managing unpredictable parasomnia behavior. Blended training also synergizes with Event Adjudication Protocol by enabling technicians to flag events accurately in real time, reducing ambiguity for subsequent dual-rater scoring and improving protocol fidelity.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Annotation-focused training diverts attention and training time from safety protocols, potentially compromising Nocturnal Safety Protocol and incident response readiness in high-risk moments. Blended training with remote expert support requires on-call senior personnel availability, increasing personnel costs and straining the core team's workload, conflicting with tight budget constraints and 3-year timeline pressures.

characterized_levers.name: Event-Triage Confidence Threshold
characterized_levers.consequences: The confidence threshold for the semi-automated event-triage tool affects the balance between sensitivity and specificity. A low threshold increases sensitivity, capturing more true events but also generating more false positives that require manual review. A high threshold increases specificity, reducing false positives but potentially missing genuine parasomnia episodes.
options: Set a low confidence threshold to maximize sensitivity and capture all potential parasomnia events, accepting a higher rate of false positives requiring manual review
Establish a high confidence threshold to minimize false positives and reduce manual review burden, even if it means potentially missing some genuine parasomnia events
Implement an adaptive threshold that adjusts based on individual participant data and overall event frequency, optimizing the balance between sensitivity and specificity
characterized_levers.review: Adjusting the confidence threshold involves a sensitivity/specificity trade-off, and the options don't address the use of multiple thresholds for different event types.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: The event-triage confidence threshold affects the balance between sensitivity and specificity, but is secondary to the overall event detection and adjudication strategies.
characterized_levers.description: Event-Triage Confidence Threshold determines the sensitivity-specificity trade-off for flagging potential parasomnia events for escalated PSG and manual review. Low thresholds maximize sensitivity and event capture, ensuring rare episodes are not missed—critical for Aim 2 longitudinal characterization and Aim 3 algorithm benchmarking with sufficient event volume. High thresholds reduce false-positive annotation burden and costs but risk missing genuine events, especially in low-frequency participants, and starve algorithm training data. Adaptive thresholds require sophisticated per-participant modeling.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Low thresholds synergize strongly with Event Detection Automation by capturing maximal training data for algorithm refinement and sensitivity benchmarking. They also support Annotation Review Depth's dual-rater system by providing sufficient event volume to justify the personnel investment and generate robust inter-rater reliability statistics required for publication credibility.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Low thresholds dramatically increase annotation workload, straining Overnight Staffing Model and Annotation Review Depth resources, pushing labor costs upward and slowing event turnaround. Adaptive thresholds require complex per-participant modeling infrastructure, competing with Data Acquisition Pipeline bandwidth and data engineer time, while risking inconsistent event capture that undermines cross-participant Aim 2 comparability.

characterized_levers.name: Control Group Stratification
characterized_levers.consequences: How the control group is stratified impacts the validity of comparisons and the generalizability of findings. Matching controls solely on age and sex may overlook other relevant factors influencing sleep patterns. More granular stratification improves the accuracy of benchmarking but increases recruitment complexity.
options: Recruit a control group matched only on age and sex to minimize recruitment burden and provide a basic comparison for nocturnal movement patterns
Stratify the control group based on age, sex, and sleep quality (e.g., PSQI score) to account for common sleep disturbances and improve benchmarking accuracy
Match controls individually to parasomnia participants based on a comprehensive set of demographic, lifestyle, and sleep-related variables to maximize comparability
characterized_levers.review: Control group stratification balances recruitment effort with benchmarking accuracy, and the options ignore the potential for using existing normative sleep data as a control.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: Control group stratification impacts the validity of comparisons, but is secondary to the overall recruitment strategy and inclusion/exclusion criteria.
characterized_levers.description: Control Group Stratification determines the matching criteria for healthy control participants recruited under identical residential monitoring conditions. This lever directly impacts the interpretability of event-triage benchmarking by establishing whether controls reflect only basic demographic similarity or account for sleep-quality variation and lifestyle factors. Stronger stratification increases recruitment complexity and timeline but improves the specificity of false-positive sensor baselines, directly supporting Aim 3's algorithmic development and reducing spurious alarm rates.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This lever strongly synergizes with Event Detection Automation and Data Acquisition Pipeline. Comprehensive control stratification provides high-quality baseline nocturnal-movement and arousal data, enabling more robust training datasets for event-triage algorithms and reducing false-positive calibration errors. Well-matched controls also enhance Data Sharing Scope by producing cleaner, more generalizable benchmark datasets suitable for public deposition.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Stratification conflicts with Participant Recruitment Channels and staffing sustainability. Matching controls on comprehensive lifestyle and sleep variables significantly increases recruitment burden, competing for limited enrollment capacity and extending timelines—potentially delaying Aim 2 phenotyping work. This tension is most acute with the timeline and participant-yield targets that gate year-two operations.

characterized_levers.name: Publication Target Breadth
characterized_levers.consequences: The breadth of publication targets influences the dissemination of research findings and the project's overall impact. Focusing solely on high-impact sleep medicine journals may limit the reach to other relevant fields. Expanding the scope to include journals in related disciplines increases dissemination but may dilute the core message.
options: Target only high-impact sleep medicine journals to maximize visibility within the core field and establish credibility within the sleep research community
Expand publication targets to include journals in neurology, psychology, and engineering to reach a broader audience and foster interdisciplinary collaboration
Prioritize open-access journals and pre-print servers to ensure wider dissemination of findings, even if it means sacrificing some prestige associated with traditional journals
characterized_levers.review: Publication breadth trades focused impact for wider dissemination, and the options don't consider the strategic use of conference presentations to build momentum.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: Publication target breadth influences dissemination, but is secondary to the core research aims and the quality of the findings.
characterized_levers.description: Publication Target Breadth sets the scope and venue strategy for disseminating study findings across peer-reviewed journals, pre-print servers, and interdisciplinary outlets. This lever influences visibility, credibility within sleep medicine, and reach into adjacent fields (neurology, engineering) that may adopt or build upon the event-triage tools. It directly shapes the project's ability to establish the residential-capture model as a methodological standard and to secure phase-two funding.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This lever synergizes strongly with Data Sharing Scope and Pharmaceutical Partnership Terms. Broader publication targets amplify reach for methods-validation and phenotyping findings, enhancing credibility for data-sharing agreements and attracting pharma partnerships. Interdisciplinary venues (neurology, engineering) accelerate adoption of the semi-automated event-triage framework beyond traditional sleep medicine, expanding the impact and sustainability argument for grant renewals.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Publication broadening conflicts with Publication Timeline and year-two milestone pressures. Targeting high-impact sleep medicine journals requires longer review cycles and higher rejection rates; expanding to open-access and interdisciplinary venues may dilute the core sleep medicine narrative, potentially weakening grant reviewer perception of disciplinary focus. This trade-off is especially acute when balancing fast publication of pilot methods-validation results against comprehensive phenotyping work.

characterized_levers.name: PSG Montage Density
characterized_levers.consequences: The density of the PSG montage during enhanced nights affects the richness of the physiological data and the burden on participants. A full high-density montage provides detailed information but can be uncomfortable and disruptive. A reduced montage is less burdensome but may miss subtle physiological markers.
options: Employ a full high-density PSG montage with numerous EEG channels, EOG, EMG, and ECG to capture the most detailed physiological data possible during enhanced nights
Utilize a reduced PSG montage with fewer EEG channels and only essential EOG and EMG leads to minimize participant discomfort and improve sleep quality
Implement an adaptive montage that adjusts based on individual participant characteristics and event frequency, optimizing the balance between data richness and participant comfort
characterized_levers.review: PSG montage density balances data richness with participant comfort, and the options overlook the potential for using wireless or dry-electrode sensors to improve comfort.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: PSG montage density directly affects the richness of the physiological data and the burden on participants, impacting data quality and participant comfort.
characterized_levers.description: PSG Montage Density specifies the electrode configuration and physiological signal richness during enhanced nights (first, mid-stay, and final nights) and escalation nights. This lever balances data quality and scientific power—denser montages capture finer neurophysiological correlates of parasomnia morphology and arousal patterns, supporting Aim 2 phenotyping—against participant comfort, sleep disruption, and logistical burden. Adaptive approaches optimize per-individual trade-offs but increase technician training and annotation complexity.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This lever strongly synergizes with Data Acquisition Pipeline and Annotation Review Depth. Higher montage density generates richer multimodal signals, improving event morphology characterization and supporting Event Detection Automation with more discriminative features. Enhanced signal diversity also enables more nuanced annotation scoring per AASM criteria, directly supporting the dual-rater reliability benchmarking required for Aim 3 validation.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Dense montages conflict with Suite Ambient Design and Overnight Staffing Model. High-density electrode leads increase visual clinical appearance, compromising the domestic feel essential for naturalistic behavior capture. Denser configurations also demand longer technician setup time, straining the 3-person rotating night team covering 8 suites safely, and may reduce participant sleep quality—directly undermining the longitudinal data yield and event-capture rates that gate year-two operations.
